tagline.text: A breezy limestone cave in Albay with a window onto Mayon

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: Sample ₱50 admission per person and ₱300 guide for 1–5. Transport extra.

children.text: Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave is a limestone cave in Cotmon, Camalig, Albay, famous for the cool wind that blows through its openings, just as its name suggests. Electric lighting and stairs make it manageable for beginners with a guide, and one opening looks out toward Mayon Volcano.

Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave sits in Cotmon village in Camalig, Albay. "Hoyop" means "blowing wind" in Bikol, and English-language sources sometimes call it Blow-Blow Cave. Cool air moves through several openings on the hillside, so even at midday the inside feels far cooler than the outside. One source puts the cave about
25km
southwest of Legazpi, while another says it is about
12km
from the center of Camalig. Reference points differ, so think of it as roughly half an hour by road from Legazpi.
The cave is known as a short guided visit. One blogger reports that it has seven large chambers but only three are open to visitors, and the normal tour covers two chambers in about
1 hour

. The remaining chambers are meant for experienced cavers. The largest chamber has a concrete floor, and stairs and simple dirt paths connect the sections. Because some parts are narrow or slippery, it is safest to move with a guide.

The cave is also layered with human history. Excavations led by the archaeologist Fr. Cantius Kobak turned up jars thought to date from about 200 BC to AD 900, and the cave is said to have been used for burials. Most of the finds are at the National Museum in Manila, and some are displayed at Camalig Church. During the Japanese occupation it served as a refuge and a hideout for Hukbalahap guerrillas, and during martial law villagers reportedly gathered here to dance and hold celebrations. Even today it serves as an evacuation shelter during typhoons.

The opening that looks toward Mayon is the cave's signature view. However, Mayon is often hidden by cloud, and one reviewer visited twice without seeing it. Rather than pinning all your hopes on the volcano view, go to enjoy the breeze and the stories of the site, and you are likely to be satisfied. Fees and operating arrangements change from year to year, so check the latest announcements.

As the name says, cool wind blows in through several openings. It is a pleasant place to escape the midday heat, and the air changes from section to section because dry and humid areas are mixed inside.
One opening is as wide as a large window, and on a clear day Mayon Volcano is visible through it. Clouds are common, so aim for early morning and the dry season.

blocks.title: Stairs and lighting along the route

children.text: This is a show cave with electric lighting, stairs and firmly packed paths, so you can walk through without special equipment. Helmets are required, and you need to duck in narrow spots.
The largest chamber has a concrete floor and is spacious enough to host events. Stalagmites and stalactites appear here and there, though some visitors find them modest compared with larger caves.
Jars and burial remains have been found here, and pottery from about 200 BC to AD 900 is described in the sources. Your guide can tell you the story of the finds.

blocks.title: Stories of war and martial law

children.text: The cave sheltered people and guerrillas during the Japanese occupation and became a place for dancing and celebrations during martial law. The village's history is layered inside it, which makes it more than an ordinary tourist stop.
The standard tour covers two chambers in about
1 hour
, and one reviewer called it a good first cave for beginners. The deeper route to the third chamber takes about
6 hours
and is said to be for experienced visitors only.

blocks.title: Souvenir shops and a café at the entrance

children.text: The approach road to the entrance reportedly has souvenir shops and a simple café. After your visit you can rest and try Bicol snacks.

items.title: Half day from Legazpi
items.subtitle: The cave and a loop around Camalig

children.text: Take a jeepney or van from Legazpi to Camalig. The usual ride is about
30–45 minutes
From the Camalig town center, take a tricycle to the cave entrance in Cotmon. One guide says it takes about
15 minutes
from town.
Register at the entrance, hire a guide and put on a helmet. Fees depend on the size of your group, so ask first.
Tour two chambers with your guide. Check the weather at the Mayon-facing opening and take photos.
Rest at the shops near the entrance and look around for snacks and souvenirs.
Head back into Camalig town for lunch and, if you like, continue to Sumlang Lake or Cagsawa Ruins.
The cave is cool, but it is hot outside. See the cave in the morning and move on to other sights in the afternoon to pace your energy.

items.title: Camalig day route
items.subtitle: Cave, lake and ruins in one day

children.text: Leave Legazpi and go to Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave first. Mornings are quieter and Mayon is more likely to be visible.
Move on to Sumlang Lake and try a bamboo raft or a kayak.
Have lunch in Camalig town and try pinangat, a Bicol specialty.
See Mayon Volcano and the partly buried old church at Cagsawa Ruins.
Return to Legazpi before sunset.
Three stops in one day make for tight timing, so depending on local traffic you may want to drop either the lake or the ruins.

By rental car or private car, take the Pan-Philippine Highway (AH26); it takes about

, and there are signs toward the cave.
You explore the cave on foot. There are stairs and dirt paths, and some sections are narrow.
One source says the cave is difficult to reach by wheelchair.
The inside of the cave is cool all year, but the walk to it and the Mayon view depend on the weather. Mayon is most visible in the dry season when clouds are fewer, and in the early morning.

In the rainy season the road to the entrance can be wet and the inside slippery, so take extra care. It is safest to check locally whether the cave is operating. Postpone your visit when a typhoon warning is in effect; the cave is also used as an evacuation shelter during typhoons.

Information about lodging near the cave is limited. Most visitors stay in Legazpi and make a round trip to Camalig. If you would like to stay in Camalig, check a booking site for availability on your dates.

Camalig is known for pinangat, a dish made from taro leaves, and a pinangat festival is reportedly held every June. After the cave, enjoy it with lunch in town. As in much of Bicol, many dishes use coconut milk and chili, so tell the cook in advance if you do not like spicy food. There are reportedly souvenir shops and a simple café near the cave entrance where you can take a light break.

A few notes for planning your visit. The inside of the cave is cool, so a light jacket helps, but the slope up to the entrance is hot and sweaty, so a spare shirt is handy. Bring plenty of small bills, since small shops may not accept cards. Ask your guide where photography is allowed. The chambers are not large, so a weekday morning is much more relaxed than a crowded weekend.
Wear sneakers or shoes with good grip. Parts of the cave are wet and slippery.
Helmets are required. Use the one the guide lends you.
Bring a small flashlight. Even with lighting, corners can be dark.
If you hope to see Mayon, go on a dry-season morning. Clouds often gather in the afternoon.

Reports say graffiti, littering, damaging the rock, drinking alcohol and dating are prohibited inside the cave. Follow the rules.
Travel light and leave large bags at your lodging.
Sumlang Lake and Cagsawa Ruins are close by, so combining them on the same day is efficient.
The cave has narrow and slippery spots. If a typhoon or heavy rain is forecast, postpone your visit, and always stay with your guide.
Only some of the seven chambers are open to visitors. Do not enter restricted sections.
Some openings require you to stoop or kneel, which can be uncomfortable if you have claustrophobia.
One source says access is difficult for wheelchair users and people with limited mobility.
Fees differ by source, so confirm them on site and ask to see a receipt or a posted rate list.
The Mayon view can be hidden by cloud, so keep your expectations modest. Check the latest announcements.
A lake in the same town of Camalig, famous for Mayon Volcano reflected on its calm water. It is easy to combine in one day, and you should confirm travel time locally.
A major sight with the remains of a church buried by the 1814 eruption of Mayon, and a good addition to the same day.
The volcano that symbolizes Albay, also visible from the cave's window opening.
